name: MP3 player
blurb: The pocket digital music player of the 2000s, from the iPod to China's Meizu and aigo
title: MP3 Players: From MPMan and iPod to Meizu, and Where They Went
description: MP3 players stored music on flash memory or tiny hard drives. Born in 1998, they boomed with the iPod and Chinese brands in the 2000s, then lost out to phones.
answer: An MP3 player is a pocket device that stores and plays digital music files, first sold in 1998 and made mainstream by Apple's iPod in 2001. In China in the mid-2000s nearly every student had one, often from local brands such as Meizu, aigo or Newsmy rather than Apple. Sales peaked around 2007, smartphones took over in the 2010s, and Apple ended the iPod line in 2022.

body: Typical Chinese MP3 players were the size of a lighter or USB stick, with a small screen, a lanyard to hang round your neck and either one AAA battery or a built-in one. You plugged it into a computer with a USB cable and dragged songs across; most doubled as a USB drive for homework files.

Early models held 128 MB or 256 MB, a few dozen songs. Many Chinese players also had FM radio, voice recording and a plain-text e-book reader, which students used for English listening practice and for reading novels under the covers. Players that could show video were widely sold in China as "MP4" players, whatever format they actually played.

iPod touch discontinued, ending the iPod line

body: Once phones could play music and go online, a separate player was one more thing to carry. iPhone sales overtook the iPod in 2011, and Apple dropped the last iPod in May 2022 after about 450 million had been sold. Meizu launched its first smartphone, the M8, in 2009 and never went back.

The category has not vanished entirely. As of 2021, Chinese makers such as aigo and Newsmy were still producing small players, and a niche of high-fidelity players for audiophiles continues. Old iPods and Chinese MP3 players now mostly change hands second-hand and among collectors.

faq.q: What was the first MP3 player?
faq.a: The MPMan F10 from South Korea's SaeHan Information Systems, on sale in spring 1998 with 32 MB or 64 MB of memory, is usually counted as the first mass-produced one.
Yes. Meizu started in 2003 as an MP3 player maker; its 2006 M6 miniPlayer was its best-known model before it switched to phones.
The iPod classic ended in 2014, the nano and shuffle in 2017, and the last model, the iPod touch, in May 2022.
